findings.summary: Eleven plural-foreground regression cases test consent, selective disclosure, contradictory foregrounds, synthetic authority, shared-rule delivery, and surveillance boundaries.
Validator enforces the invariant that a shared world does not imply shared attention and that active shared rules remain human-consented and reversible.
Newest-first public record closes the September 16 contribution rather than leaving the regression suite as an unregistered code artifact.
Horizon advances beyond plural-foreground validation toward productive disagreement and parallel construction.
External search did not expose reliable indexed TRY IT or Terraria pages during this sweep; repository-backed public assets remain the inspectable canonical source for the cycle.
No appropriately authorized live D1 write action is available in the active execution context, so no live backfill or migration-state claim is made.
findings.d1_action: When an authorized live D1 path is available, register the new fixtures, validator, build entry, daily record, next edge, and supported relationships/tags using canonical repo pointers rather than duplicating payloads.

privacy_boundary: No private dialogue, secret configuration, token, credential, or private environment payload was inspected or copied during reconciliation.
